title: Modifying Driver Behavior with Callbacks
description: Inject a parity error and a delay into one of two drivers with a callback hook, without altering the driver class, then break the attachment on purpose and stack two callbacks.

steps.title: Step 1: Review the hook and the two drivers
steps.instructions: Open `testbench.sv` and locate the `packet_driver_cb` virtual class, the `uvm_do_callbacks` call inside the driver's `run_phase`, the `a_parity_ok` checker in `packet_if`, and the two drivers `env.drv0` and `env.drv1`. Note which packet fields the driver reads after the hook returns. Run the starter once: six `DRV` lines with `error=0 delay_cycles=0`, no `PARITY_ERR`, and `display()` reports no callbacks for `packet_driver`.

steps.title: Step 2: Implement the Callback
steps.instructions: Create a class `error_inject_cb` extending `packet_driver_cb`. Override the function `pre_drive(packet_driver driver, packet pkt)` to set `pkt.inject_parity_error = 1` and `pkt.extra_delay_cycles = 2`.

steps.title: Step 3: Attach it to drv0 only
steps.instructions: Write `my_test::connect_phase`: create the callback and attach it to `env.drv0` only with the static `add()` of `uvm_callbacks#(packet_driver, packet_driver_cb)`. Run: `display()` lists the callback on `uvm_test_top.env.drv0` only; there are 3 `CB` messages, 3 `DRV` lines from drv0 with `error=1 delay_cycles=2` and 3 clean ones from drv1, and 3 `PARITY_ERR` errors, all from `vif0`. The third error appears only because the test sets a 20 ns drain time before dropping its objection.

steps.title: Step 4: Break it on purpose
steps.instructions: Move the callback's creation and `add()` into `my_test::build_phase`, right after `env` is created, and change the `final_phase` delete to `delete(null, my_cb)`. Predict the counts and the `display()` output, then run. Expect 6 `CB` lines, 6 `PARITY_ERR` errors (3 from `vif0`, 3 from `vif1`) and a type-wide `(*)` row in `display()`: `env.drv0` was still null, so `add()` registered the callback for every `packet_driver`. Explain why one driver alone could not reveal this mistake, then restore `connect_phase`.

steps.title: Step 5 (optional): Stack and switch
steps.instructions: Split the callback into `delay_cb` (sets `extra_delay_cycles = 2`) and `parity_err_cb` (sets `inject_parity_error = 1`, counts its packets and calls `callback_mode(0)` on itself after the second). Add `parity_err_cb` to `env.drv0`, then `delay_cb` with `UVM_PREPEND`. Predict the order in `display()` and the error count, then run: `delay_cb` is listed first, all 3 drv0 packets are delayed, and there are exactly 2 `PARITY_ERR` errors, both from `vif0`.
